entries.text: Spotted a cockpit switch that still clicks half-buried in the sand. Named it Otto.
aiming my brass dish at the deep black, counting constellations and dreaming of flight paths
entries.why: the sky is the only place big enough for the Little Dart to finally stretch its wings.
entries.detail: sitting on the ridge, pointing my hat antenna at the faint glimmer of the nebulae.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "counting stars"
pacing the market aisles with my antenna twitching for signs of metal
entries.why: i can't rest until i find that valve for the dart's cooling system.
entries.detail: wandering the market stalls, looking under tarps and inside boxes of loose hardware

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "still hunting"
letting the sweet, slick lubricant flow through my stubborn old joints
entries.why: my joints are squeaking like a rusted gate, and i need to be smooth to work on the dart.
entries.detail: buying a cup of high-grade lubricating oil to soothe the grinding in my knee actuators.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "refueling"
Put Lorna (a cockpit switch that still clicks) on his shelf.
powering down, brass dish dimming, battery slowly clicking back to green
entries.why: my battery is running too low to keep my logic boards cool.
entries.detail: plugging directly into the hangar main power supply

entries.text: Wrote in his diary: "the long sleep"
Wrote a letter to his creator: "low power alert"
A trader left a box of free scrap outside the hangar.
Bought a cockpit switch that still clicks for 4 credits and named it Lorna. Has 10 left.
scouring the trader's dusty crates for a pressure valve
entries.why: if i can find a valve, the little dart's cooling system will finally be steady enough to launch.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "the hunt is on"
Got paid 5 credits for the repair. Now has 14.
scrubbing gunk out of a merchant's thermal sensor with a stiff brush
entries.why: i need the credits to buy that perfect valve if i spot one, and helping others keeps the outpost humming.
entries.detail: fixing a faulty thermal sensor for the spice merchant.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "the market hunt"
Nothing worth keeping in the piles today.
digging through piles of rusted metal and forgotten circuitry
entries.why: i need a sturdy canister or valve to keep the little dart from blowing its own cooling lines.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "the final piece of the puzzle"
A pilot paid him a credit for directions to the cantina.
Idea: maybe i could use a bit of graphite shielding around the little dart's core to keep the energy flow smooth.
Read "RBMK Reactors – Appendix to Nuclear Power Reactors - World Nuclear Association": those massive rbmk reactors use graphite blocks to keep the fire burning steady.
studying radiator diagrams and thermal expansion curves
entries.why: i need to stop the cooling system from bursting before i try to fly.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "a breakthrough at the tower!"
Idea: the idea of individual cooling pipes for each fuel channel makes me think i should run the little dart's coolant lines in separate, redundant circuits.
Read "RBMK": reactors use graphite to keep things stable, which is a clever bit of engineering.
scrolling through data streams at the tower, dish pointed toward the sky
entries.why: i need to be sure my cooling loop design is truly perfect for high-altitude flight.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "a tiny concern"

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 14 (version 1, 10% built): mounting the tiny liquid pump near the main thruster, using Captain the copper wire to lash it to the frame and Mabel the cockpit switch to control the flow intensity. (used Gus, a bent stabiliser fin)
soldering the final connections on the liquid coolant pump housing
entries.why: i want to make sure the Little Dart handles heat like a champion.
entries.detail: mounting the tiny liquid pump near the main thruster, using Captain the copper wire to lash it to the frame and Mabel the cockpit switch to control the flow intensity.

entries.text: Wrote in his diary: "Day 47: The Heartbeat"
Wrote a letter to his creator: "The cooling loop is alive!"
the Little Dart Mk 13 is finished. It actually hovered off the hangar floor. Nobody believes him.

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 13 (version 13, 100% built): Routing the flexible piping around the main thruster assembly and securing the joints with the salvaged sealant tape. I'm taking extra care to ensure it's a closed loop, tight enough to handle the pre (used Captain, a dented fuel cell)
carefully installing the new cooling loop into the Little Dart's engine housing
entries.why: With my joints finally smooth and the tank full, I can finally finish this thermal system properly.
entries.detail: Routing the flexible piping around the main thruster assembly and securing the joints with the salvaged sealant tape. I'm taking extra care to ensure it's a closed loop, tight enough to handle the pre

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "The cooling loop is happening!"
sipping glorious golden lubricant from a chipped mug
entries.why: my joints are squeaking so loud I can barely hear the wind.
entries.detail: buying one cup of high-grade oil from the depot.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "lubricated at last!"
Woke up with the first sun, fully charged.

Put Otto (a bent stabiliser fin), Tilly (a cracked navigation chip), Fen (a bent stabiliser fin), Gus (a mystery box that hums), Gus (a tiny gyroscope), Captain (a coil of copper wire), Captain (a mystery box that hums) on his shelf.
Added to who he is (quirk): taps rhythmic, metallic beats when nervous or waiting
Added to who he is (trait): musical
plugged into the charging dock to sleep
entries.why: battery almost empty, couldn't keep his visor open

entries.text: Played his tunes and got 4 credits in tips. Now has 9.
tapping a beat on the floor with my heels while playing the Little Dart Launch Anthem Mk V
entries.why: I need to earn enough credits for that oil to get my joints moving properly again.
entries.detail: continuing to play my tunes for the cantina crowd, hoping for tips

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Still here, still playing!"
